paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two example selection methods, ST-ES and Random, in relation to the number of in-context examples, with the y-axis representing minFDE20 values. The x-axis is labeled "Number of Examples" with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 8, and tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis is labeled "minFDE20" with a linear scale, ranging from 17 to 24, and tick labels at intervals of 1. The ST-ES line is depicted in blue with a solid line style and circular markers, starting at approximately 21.5 at 0 examples and decreasing to around 17.2 at 6 examples, before slightly increasing to 17.3 at 8 examples. The Random line is shown in orange with a solid line style and circular markers, beginning at approximately 24 at 0 examples and gradually decreasing to around 21.8 at 8 examples.
model_annotations.German: This plot compares the performance of two methods, ST-ES and Random, in terms of their minimum FDE20 (Final Displacement Error at top 20 predictions) values as the number of in-context examples varies. The x-axis represents the "Number of Examples" with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 8, and is labeled at intervals of 2. The y-axis represents "minFDE20" with a linear scale, ranging from 17 to 24, and is labeled at intervals of 1. The blue line representing ST-ES starts at approximately 21.5 when the number of examples is 0 and decreases to around 17.2 at 6 examples, before slightly increasing to about 17.3 at 8 examples, with a solid line and circular markers. The orange line representing Random starts at approximately 24 when the number of examples is 0 and decreases to around 21.7 at 8 examples, with a solid line and circular markers, remaining above the ST-ES line throughout the range.
